  "format_version": "proposed_assay/1.0",
  "id": "rna_age_encoding",
  "title": "Paired-well RNA-age sequencing with a non-poly(A) surface-reporter branch",
  "biological_question": "How does gene-specific RNA made during a defined pulse and surviving until harvest vary with the measured surface-protein phenotype of the same individual cell? This is a proposed assay architecture, not a validated protocol or an accomplished invention.",
  "measurement": "Requester requirements retained: joint newly synthesized RNA and cell-surface protein identity in individual cells; readout includes sequencing and uses existing sequencing equipment. Accessible reagents/equipment and preserving distinct justified ideas are preferences. This candidate independently develops the RNA-age-encoding direction. Assumptions introduced here: viable metabolically labelable mammalian cells; polyadenylated RNA rather than every nascent/noncoding RNA; defined ex vivo 4sU pulse; antibody-defined known surface targets rather than de novo protein sequence; plate isolation. A HeLa/4T1 CD29 species-mixing benchmark is a proposed first test, not a specified specimen or evidence of 4sU compatibility. Biological quantities are gene-specific recovered RNA counts/new-RNA fractions and surface-target identity per cell. Molecules initiated before the pulse can incorporate label if they elongate during it; the assay does not observe exact transcript initiation times. Molecules acted on are endogenous 4sU-containing RNA, bead DNA primers, and antibody-associated synthetic reporter DNA. IAA changes RNA pairing behavior; RT converts that mark into sequence information. Surface reporters use a defined non-poly(A) H tail and are separated before IAA, with both branches retained in paired physical wells until matching B_j codes are copied into DNA. The existing Illumina instrument directly reads RNA-derived and reporter-derived DNA base sequences/qualities; it does not directly observe RNA birth or protein sequence. Gene identity, pulse-born RNA probability, target identity and same-cell pairing are inferred using reference sequences, experimentally calibrated errors, binding specificity and the well/barcode dictionary. RNA UMIs support counts of recovered copies, while reporter amplicon counts support controlled identity calls without absolute protein counts. A single pulse does not determine synthesis/degradation rates.",
  "expected_benefit": "Conditional benefit: physical chemistry separation could retain a larger fraction of cells with both an informative RNA-age profile and reliable surface-target calls at matched total sequencing effort, by making reporter handling independent of RNA alkylation and preventing shared poly(A)-capture competition. There is no measured gain. IAA damage to DNA reporters or a substantial shared-capture bottleneck has not been established, so a split is useful only if the net joint measurement improves. Closest retrieved components are CITE-seq for shared transcript/surface-reporter sequencing and NASC-seq for plate-based single-cell bead RNA alkylation. SPARC is a component precedent for separating an mRNA-bead fraction from the same cell's protein-containing supernatant; its protein readout differs. The inspected scNT-seq2 report already improves second-strand copying, and the 2025 chemistry benchmark shows bead/platform-dependent outcomes. Their reported gains are not claimed as new here. Bounded atlas searches and external searches for nascent/new RNA with CITE-seq, surface markers, AbSeq and SLAM/TimeLapse did not verify the requested same-cell joint implementation. This remains an unresolved prior-art search result, not evidence of absence, novelty or impossibility; papers with separate RNA and protein experiments do not establish a joint measurement. Most serious failure: selective reporter withdrawal and pre-IAA washes lose or bias enough RNA, or transfer reporters to wrong paired wells, that fewer cells yield correctly paired measurements even though each surviving branch looks good. Other risks include 4sU toxicity/phenotype shifts, pulse smearing during handling, altered antibody affinity, ambient DNA, residual DTT suppressing alkylation, RT inhibition, inadequate uridines in short inserts, first-copy errors and UMI/barcode collisions. Discriminating experiment: randomize the same independently identifiable cell mixture and reporter clones across (A) this H-tail paired-well split, (B) a deliberately constructed same-cell shared-poly(A)-capture/IAA comparator, and (C) chemistry-free matched versions of both reporter designs. Comparator B is an engineered control, not a claimed historical method. Include RNA-only NASC-like wells and conventional CITE-seq for modality recovery references; use optimized scNT-seq2 as an additional competing RNA readout where feasible. Keep specimen/pulse, antibody clones, input-cell denominator and total RNA-plus-reporter read budget matched; downsample to equal informative read allocations as a second analysis. Include no-label, no-encoding, no-antibody/isotype, target-positive/negative and empty-well controls; labeled/unlabeled sequence-distinguishable RNA standards; distinct H-DNA standards; recorded single-cell occupancy and blinded checkerboard transfers. Measure fraction of all isolated cells yielding correctly species-paired informative RNA and target calls, recovered RNA UMIs/genes and true-new standard sensitivity at the same false-new rate, target discrimination, reporter cross-capture and wrong-cell assignment, branch recovery/mass balance, cost and cells processed per operator time. Interaction with the no-chemistry arms distinguishes chemistry isolation from tail/capture effects. Reject the proposed advantage if paired-well processing has no net joint gain or if a gain requires higher false-new/target-background rates; improved ADT counts alone are insufficient. Equipment: standard existing Illumina sequencer, cell sorter or validated single-cell plate dispenser, magnet, thermal cycler and routine liquid handling; optional plate automation. No new sequencer is proposed. Custom H-tail antibody conjugates, barcoded biotinylated RNA primers, matched reporter primers, barcode-end-retaining library geometry and a checked plate-pairing process require engineering/validation. Plate handling sacrifices throughput and adds transfers relative to droplet CITE/scNT implementations. No concentrations, optimized settings or readiness claim are supplied.",

  "id": "physical_rna_selection",
  "title": "Pre-click routing of surface reporters with pooled selection of cell-indexed EU-RNA hybrids",
  "biological_question": "For each individual cell, which polyadenylated genes produced recoverable RNA during a defined EU pulse, and which validated surface-protein targets were present at sampling? This is an untested assay architecture, not an accomplished invention or validated protocol.",
  "measurement": "Requester requirements: joint newly synthesized RNA and cell-surface protein identity in individual cells; sequencing must be included and use existing sequencing equipment. Soft preferences are accessible preparation reagents/equipment and distinct ideas when justified. Introduced choices: EU pulse labeling, plate-isolated cultured HeLa/4T1 benchmark cells, sequencing antibody-DNA reporters, poly(A)-dependent RNA capture, physical reporter routing and bound/unbound RNA libraries. These are not requester constraints. Biological quantities are recovered pulse-window polyadenylated RNA by gene and surface-target identities/relative reporter signals per singlet. The molecules acted on are EU-bearing RNA and antibody-associated DNA. The sequencer directly observes copied DNA nucleotide reads, cell/UMI codes, target codes and fraction indices. The RNA label is not copied as an obligatory mutation: label-linked hybrids are physically selected, and a library index later records that selection. Gene identity is inferred by transcript alignment; protein identity is inferred through a validated antibody-to-target lookup. Surface protein molecules are not themselves sequenced. Selected counts are not absolute synthesis rates, and unbound RNA is not pure old RNA. Label incorporation, RNA turnover during the pulse, polyadenylation, RT, recovery and selection all affect the observed subset. New/total fractions require calibration; rates need additional timepoints and a model. Prior-art finding: primary passages establish CITE-seq joint total-RNA/surface-reporter measurement and scEU-seq single-cell labeled-RNA hybrid separation. The bounded atlas and external searches did not verify a completed same-cell new-RNA/surface-protein assay; this leaves the requested combination's prior demonstration unresolved and is not a novelty claim. No suitable whole-method predecessor was established. Searches included nascent RNA/surface proteins, newly synthesized RNA/CITE-seq, metabolic labeling/CITE-seq, scEU-seq/surface, scSLAM-seq/surface and index sorting. scNT-seq2 was read as a competing conversion-based implementation; its reported library improvements are not claimed here. SCITO-seq retrieval barriers prevented a registered technical passage, so it supplies no candidate evidence. History retrieval for cite_seq failed because source IDs were missing from the supplied registry; no absence-of-precursor inference is made. Only the inspected node-description windows and cited primary passages support the component comparison; uninspected atlas reviews and supplements do not support new claims.",
  "expected_benefit": "If successful, dedicated reporter routing before EU click/streptavidin processing would permit surface reporters to avoid potentially incompatible RNA preparation and allow sequencing to favor recent RNA without spending most RNA reads on unselected transcripts. Shared cell codes would reunite independently sequenced branches. The improvement claimed for testing is joint informative-RNA recovery and reporter fidelity at matched total sequencing effort, not the mere combination of RNA and protein measurements. Damage or loss in an unbranched joint workflow has not been demonstrated; the benefit can be zero. Most serious failure: reporter capture and off-cell single-cell RNA cleanup deplete/degrade low-copy labeled RNA, and labeled RNA no longer carries its original indexed cDNA through selection. Apparent enrichment could then coexist with worse informative molecules per input cell or false age/cell assignments. Other costs are imperfect label incorporation, length/label-position bias, nonspecific RNA/reporter binding, extra wells and transfers, repeated reporter copying, reduced throughput and a less reliable total-RNA denominator. Equipment: existing paired-end Illumina sequencing, a single-cell sorter, plate magnet, thermocycler and routine liquid handling. No new sequencing instrument is proposed. Custom non-poly(A) antibody conjugates, non-biotin cell-coded capture supports, matching primer sets, low-input cleanup and read-layout validation are unresolved engineering needs; accessible components do not make this a ready kit. The decisive end-to-end comparison and rejection criteria are recorded in operation:ps_route and operation:ps_decode. No wet-lab results are asserted.",

      "earlier_arrangement": "CITE-seq uses poly(A)-tailed reporter DNA and polyadenylated RNA at a shared poly(T) capture/indexing interface, then separates amplified reporter-derived and RNA-derived DNA. That reported assay does not measure an RNA synthesis window.",
      "retained": "Antibody-associated target codes, nucleotide sequencing and a common cell-code namespace joining RNA and reporter observations.",
      "changed": "Replace reporter poly(A) capture with an orthogonal docking tail on a non-biotin reporter support; isolate cells in mapped wells, attach reporter cell codes, physically remove that branch before RNA click, and later attach the matching code to RNA cDNA before RNA pooling. This is a proposed design relationship to component nodes, not an established historical extension.",
      "expected_gain": "If chemical exposure or shared capture limits a joint workflow, early routing could improve reporter retention and new-RNA information per read. Extra capture/transfer losses may eliminate that gain; compare both per input cell and per retained paired cell."
    },
    {
      "id": "ps_change_selection_order",
      "earlier_refs": [],
      "proposed_target_ids": [
        "operation:ps_sort_lyse",
        "operation:ps_click",
        "operation:ps_rt",
        "operation:ps_pool",
        "operation:ps_select",
        "operation:ps_make_rna_libraries"
      ],
      "earlier_arrangement": "The retrieved scEU-seq overview biotinylates RNA in fixed/permeabilized cells before sorting and RT, then separates pooled indexed hybrids into two fractions. It is a literature component precedent, not an atlas record or a demonstrated surface-protein coassay.",
      "retained": "EU-dependent RNA affinity selection, cell indexing before pooled separation, and explicit selected/unbound fraction libraries.",
      "changed": "Measure surface binding on live cells, route reporters in isolated lysates, move RNA cleanup/click into separate mapped RNA daughters, and only then form and pool indexed hybrids. RNA remains the affinity-bearing substrate; fraction provenance is transferred to library indices after selection.",
      "expected_gain": "Would isolate surface-reporter processing from RNA selection and permit intentional new-RNA read allocation. It adds single-cell cleanup loss and handling; in-situ performance does not establish this off-cell transfer."
    }
